title: TE Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension
disposition_detail: All five specifications were sustained. Presbytery was instructed to reexamine TE Kurt Lutjens, preserve a complete transcript, report by November 10, 1986, and pursue orderly discipline after pastoral counsel if nonconformity continued.
first_summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery’s clarification that Lutjens had changed his sacramental views, alleging that it contradicted the facts and retroactively rewrote Presbytery’s minutes. All five specifications were sustained, including improper interpretation of BCO 58-4. Presbytery was ordered to reexamine Lutjens, record the examination, and report to the judicial committee; continued nonconformity would require orderly discipline.
summary: Presbytery’s response claiming that Lutjens had changed his sacramental views was challenged as factually false and as a retroactive rewriting of minutes Presbytery had previously refused to interpret. All five specifications were sustained, including illegitimate interpretation of BCO 58-4. Because the earlier examination transcript was unavailable through mechanical failure, Presbytery was ordered to reexamine Lutjens, provide a complete transcript, and report by November 10, 1986. Discipline remained conditional on continued nonconformity after pastoral counsel.

sources.supports: Adjudication, five specifications, remedial instructions, reasons, deadline, and conditional discipline.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Title and adjudication appear at lines 1, 53–55; the conclusion identifies the commission and records adoption followed by reconsideration and recommittal at lines 119–121.
evidence_notes.dispute: Presbytery’s challenged clarification and the five issues are stated at lines 59–75, printed p. 154.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The five sustained specifications appear at lines 77–91; reexamination was required because the prior transcript was lost through mechanical failure, lines 93–97.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Neither malice nor negligence caused the missing transcript; discipline was required only if reexamination showed continued nonconformity, lines 95 and 115–117.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The adjudication reproduces the Eleventh General Assembly’s governing directives and explains their binding effect under BCO 14-7, lines 99–111.
